title: Rolling Upgrade Safety Net & Preflight Checklist for LTS/Canary Channels
creator: Claire Kim
description:
Goal: Create a reproducible, low-latency preflight that runs automatically for rolling upgrades across LTS and canary channels. The safety net must detect functional regressions (smoke/e2e), performance regressions (per-model token latency and throughput), and quality regressions (eval suites and a small set of human-reviewed prompts) before any automated step escalates to wider rollout.

Scope:
- Preflight harness that runs against target cluster(s) and verifies model variant compatibility, KV cache warming, and quantized kernel fallbacks.
- Canary gating rules for auto-rollout: pass smoke -> pass perf gates -> pass evals -> ramp.
- A compact, fast eval suite (<= 30 min total wall time) for continuous protection on frequent releases and a deeper nightly suite for major/minor releases.
- Instrumentation and dashboards showing signal-level pass/fail and trend windows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full eval (long, more coverage) vs compact eval (fast, risk of missing edge regressions). Chose: compact preflight for automated gating + nightly full eval for LTS candidates.
- Run per-model end-to-end tests in isolated cluster vs run against canary instances on same cluster. Chose isolated lightweight harness to avoid noisy neighbors but include a final in-cluster sanity check.

Acceptance summary: This ticket establishes the checklist, CI job definitions, Prometheus queries for gating, and links to runbooks/PRs. Implementation work is split into two follow-ups: infra automation (ENG-42652) and eval-suite authoring (ENG-42653).
acceptance_criteria: Automated preflight job (preflight-rolling-1.20) triggers as part of release pipeline and completes within 40 minutes
Smoke tests: all basic API behaviors (generation, streaming, tool-calls, embeddings) pass against canary model variants
Perf gates: p50/p95/p99 token-latency and QPS compared to baseline — fail if p99 increases > 12% or throughput drops > 15% for any pinned model
Eval suite: compact test of 250 seed prompts per model with pass/fail thresholds (exact match/semantic thresholds) and a human review queue for flagged regressions
Rollback policy wired: any preflight failure blocks rollout and creates an incident with runbook link
Dashboards and alerting: gate failure alerts to #release-safety and on-call SRE, with links to traces and failing examples

testing_matrix: Smoke tests (fast): API sanity for generation, embeddings, function-calls, and structured output (approx 3 minutes)
KV cache migration probe: verify prefix-warm start across 10 queries and ensure cache hit rate > 85% after warmup
Perf microbench: 5-minute constant QPS ramp for each model at target sequence length percentiles (16, 128, 1024) with p50/p95/p99 latency collection
Quality eval (compact): 250 prompts covering NLU, coding, math, and safety. Metrics: BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding similarity thresholds for semantic checks
Fallbacks: test auto-fallback to quantized variant when FP16 kernel causes OOM; verify correctness on sample prompts
rollout_plan: 1) Preflight job runs against isolated canary cluster (automated). If pass ->
2) Small in-cluster sanity check (10% of canaries) to validate networking and auth paths
3) Canary ramp to 5% traffic for 30 minutes with live telemetry monitoring
4) If no regressions, ramp to 25% for 1 hour; run secondary compact eval at 25%
5) Final automated gate: if all checks green, proceed to LTS candidate promotion; otherwise trigger rollback and create incident
rollback_steps: Immediate: abort rollout and mark release as blocked in pipeline
2: Trigger automated rollback script to pin previous model version and restore routing (scripts/rollback/pin-prev.sh)
3: Notify #release-safety, on-call SRE, and responsible release engineer with failed gate details and link to dashboard
4: Capture logs, traces (Profiler + KV cache heatmap), and failing prompt samples for postmortem
5: Schedule hotfix/patch release or revert based on postmortem decision
monitoring_queries: SQL (ClickHouse): SELECT model, quantileExact(0.99)(latency_ms) FROM token_latency WHERE timestamp > now() - interval 30 minute GROUP BY model
Trace search: traces where status!=200 AND span.operation="generate" since 30m
Eval diff query: compare baseline pass-rate with current run; fail if absolute drop > 5% or relative drop > 12%
notes: Follow-ups: ENG-42652 (CI automation for preflight), ENG-42653 (compact eval authoring), ENG-42654 (runbook drilling and pager rota).
We intentionally limit compact eval to ~250 prompts to keep wall time acceptable for frequent micro-releases; nightly full eval will run on LTS branches.
Consideration: add token-level synthetic load tests during preflight to detect regression in KV cache eviction behavior (future work).
PM feedback: allow per-customer sensitivity tuning and an opt-out for non-critical model updates.
